The Main module is part of the framework, and the Event Manager interacts directly with application handlers. It features an Event Queue and a base Handler component extended by standard and application-specific handlers.

architectural_approaches.approach_name: Event-driven framework with a single Event Manager and a single Event Queue
architectural_approaches.description: The supplied architecture describes an event framework in which the Main module is part of the framework, the Event Manager interacts directly with application handlers, event processing uses one Event Queue, and quantitative limits specify one Event Manager and one Event Queue. The runtime constraints also indicate FIFO dispatch, idle waiting for input, and sequential event processing on a single processor.

addressed_attributes.rationale: The explicit Event Manager, Event Queue, base Handler component, and direct interaction with application handlers provide the mechanism for event processing and component interaction described in the inputs.
A single queue and sequential processing imply a simple event flow, though the supplied model also notes qualitative slowness due to the number of components involved.
FIFO dispatch and a defined STOP handler indicate controlled processing behavior, but the inputs do not provide failure-handling mechanisms beyond that.
Base Handler extension by standard and application-specific handlers suggests some variation points for adding functionality.
A base Handler component and framework services may be reused in future projects, although the tight interdependence between framework and application logic limits this.
